title: Successor update of counted frequencies
statement: Let $A$ be counting-sort arguments, let $kf\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ assign a key to each index, and let $i\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose an integer-valued memory map $\mu'$ has value $0$ at address $A.cnt$, and for every key $t<A.nb$ has at address $A.cnt+(t+1)$ the number of indices $j<i$ with $kf(j)=t$. Change the value at address $A.cnt+(kf(i)+1)$ to one more than the number of indices $j<i$ with $kf(j)=kf(i)$, leaving every other address unchanged. The resulting memory map has value $0$ at $A.cnt$, and at each address $A.cnt+(t+1)$ for $t<A.nb$ it stores the number of indices $j<i+1$ with $kf(j)=t$.
hypotheses_covered: the memory value at $A.cnt$ is zero
for every $t<A.nb$, the memory value at $A.cnt+(t+1)$ counts indices $j<i$ with $kf(j)=t$
replaced:
Let $A$ be counting-sort arguments, let $kf\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ assign a key
to each index, and let $i\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose a memory state $\mu'$ satisfies
$\mu'(A.cnt)=0$ and, for every key $t<A.nb$, its cell at address $A.cnt+(t+1)$ contains
the number of indices $j<i$ whose key is $t$. Then the state obtained from $\mu'$ by
setting the cell at address $A.cnt+(kf(i)+1)$ to one more than the number of indices
$j<i$ whose key is $kf(i)$, while leaving all other cells unchanged, satisfies these
same conditions for the first $i+1$ indices.
